init.instructions: CADCraft is a 2D/3D CAD drafting app (an AutoCAD clone). Coordinates are drawing units, y up. Fastest path: command_line with AutoCAD syntax, e.g. `line 0,0 10,0 10,5 c`, `circle 5,2.5 1`, `rectang 0,0 4,3`, `offset 1` then pick, `zoom e`. Or execute with JSON (list_commands shows ids and params). Verify with inspect_drawing / query_entities and look with render. Backend: headless CADCraft session.

Starts commands by name or alias (LINE, L, CIRCLE, C, PLINE, RECTANG, MOVE, TRIM, OFFSET, ZOOM…) and answers the active prompt: points `x,y`, relative `@dx,dy`, polar `@dist<angle`, distances, keywords (e.g. `c` for Close), empty text = Enter. Spaces act as Enter, so `circle 0,0 5` works in one call. Returns the new prompt and command-line output, and `error` when the line was refused.

init.instructions: DeckCraft is a presentation app (a PowerPoint clone). Coordinates are points on the current slide (y down; the default 16:9 slide is 960×540). Every action is a command: find ids and parameters with list_commands and run them with run_command (or several with batch). Typical flow: new_presentation → add_slide {layout:"titleAndContent", title, body} → add_shape / add_text_box / insert_picture / insert_chart → inspect_slide to read back ids, boxes and text → render_slide to look at the result. Save with save_presentation (.deckcraft or .pptx). Backend: headless (in-process engine; no window). init.instructions: DesignCraft is a page-layout app (an InDesign clone). Coordinates are points in spread space (y down; on a single-page spread the page's top-left is (0,0); a default Letter page is 612×792). Every action is a command: find ids and parameters with list_commands and run them with execute (or several with batch). Typical flow: new_document → execute frame.create {rect:[x0,y0,x1,y1], content:"text", text:"…"} → set_story_text / execute type.char / style.paragraph.apply → render_page to look at the result. inspect_document lists pages, items (ids, bounds), stories (overset) and styles. place_image puts a picture on the page. Backend: headless (in-process engine, no window). Community: https://discord.gg/artcraft (Discord), https://getartcraft.com/apps/designcraft (app page), https://github.com/storytold/designcraft (source). The `app.links` command returns these links.

init.instructions: EffectCraft is an After Effects-class motion graphics compositor. Everything is an engine command: command_list discovers ids and params, command_run {id, params} runs them (undoable; command_batch runs several in order). Typical flow: command_run comp.new -> command_run layer.newText / layer.newSolid (returns the layer id) -> set_property / add_keyframe -> command_run effect.apply -> render_preview to look at the result. Inspect with doc_inspect, get_project, get_comp and get_layer (every property node carries its `path`, e.g. `transform/position`, `effects/#1/blurriness`). Times are seconds. In bridge mode (app started with `--control <port>`) screenshot and the ui_* tools show and operate the live window.

Every menu item, shortcut and panel gesture maps to one of these ids; run them with execute_command. Narrow with `filter` (e.g. `layer.new`, `keys`, `effect`).

init.instructions: FigCraft is an interface design tool (Figma-class): pages hold frames, groups, shapes, text, components and instances, with auto layout, styles, variables and prototyping. Coordinates are page units (1 unit = 1 px at 100% zoom), x right and y DOWN. create_node and set_properties take x/y RELATIVE TO THE PARENT (the page when there is no parent, so page coordinates); inspect_document reports both x/y relative to the parent frame (groups don't count) and absoluteBounds in page coordinates. Children of an auto-layout frame are positioned by the layout (set layout, gap, padding, mainAlign, crossAlign, sizingH/sizingV instead). Every menu item, panel action and shortcut is a command: find ids and params with list_commands (use a filter) and run them with run_command, or several as one undo step with batch. Commands act on `ids` when given, else on the selection; new layers become the selection. Colours are "#RRGGBB" or "#RRGGBBAA". Verify your work: inspect_document / get_node return the layer tree as JSON (check sizes, fills, layout, overrides), and screenshot returns a PNG of the page or of given layers to look at. undo/redo step through history. Resources: figcraft://document, figcraft://node/{id}, figcraft://command/{id}. prompts/list has workflows. Backend: headless (in-process engine session; no window). Files: only these folders may be read: ["<CRAFT_RADICE>\\progetti","<CRAFT_RADICE>\\progetti"]; written: ["<CRAFT_RADICE>\\progetti"] (any other path is refused).

Every menu item, panel action and shortcut is a command; run one with run_command (or several as one undo step with batch). Most commands act on `ids` when given, else on the selection. Use `filter` to narrow (e.g. "align", "layout", "variable", "style", "component", "proto").

init.instructions: LightCraft is a non-destructive photo library and raw developer (a Lightroom alternative). Photos have integer ids; most editing acts on the *active* photo (`set_develop`, `crop` and `export` with an explicit photo id end the current edit interaction, replace the selection with that one photo and make it active; `get_develop` and `render_photo` do not change the selection). Typical loop: query_photos → select_photos (or pass id) → list_controls → set_develop {values: {"light.exposure": 0.5}} → render_preview to look at the result → export. Positions (crop rects, mask points, brush strokes) are normalized image coordinates 0..1 with the origin at the top-left. Every action is a command: command_list shows ids and parameter docs; command_run {id, params} runs any of them; command_batch runs steps in order. Inspect with doc_inspect. Edits are undoable (undo / redo). Backend: headless.

tools.description: Render and write photos. Give `path` (one photo; format from the extension unless `format` is set) or `dir` (batch, file names from `naming`). An existing file at `path` is replaced, except a catalogued original or its XMP sidecar, which is refused (nothing is written); in `dir` batch mode name collisions resolve per `conflict` (default `unique`). init.instructions: PdfCraft edits PDFs. Open a file with doc_open to get a document id, then inspect (doc_info, text_extract, text_find, page_render) or edit it (page_*, doc_set_info). Edits are undoable (edit_undo) and stay in memory until doc_save. Page numbers are 1-based. Open documents are also resources: pdfcraft://doc/{doc}/info, /text, /page/{page}/text and /page/{page}/image. command_list discovers command ids and tool schemas; command_run executes one, command_batch runs several. doc_inspect returns open document state; render_preview returns a bounded PNG.

tools.description: Run convert, ocr and/or optimize over files and folders, one file at a time. recursive defaults to false. Preserve paths relative to each selected folder inside out_dir; duplicate inputs run once. Skip unsupported files, links and the output subtree. Existing outputs receive numbered names and are never replaced. Continue after per-file errors unless stop_on_error is true. Return completed/failed/skipped counts and per-file results. Discovery is bounded to 10000 entries and 64 folder levels. Convert must be first; each step can appear once. OCR uses installed models. Optimize uses Reduce File Size settings, optionally overriding target ppi (threshold 1.5 times ppi) and JPEG quality; a larger candidate keeps the original bytes. Sources and open documents are unchanged.

Returns a JSON array (no wrapper object) of {id, label, menu: [path], shortcut: string|null, params: doc string, enabled: bool, disabledReason: string|null, needsDocument: bool}. `disabledReason` says why a command is off (null when enabled); `needsDocument` is true when it is off because no document is open: create or open one first (doc_new, doc_open).

tools.name: command_run
tools.title: Command run
tools.description: Run an engine command by id with JSON params (see command_list). Returns the command's JSON result. Long commands (filters, Content-Aware Fill/Scale, Photomerge, brush import) wait to finish unless `wait` is false: then they run as a background job and the result is {job: id} (see jobs_list, jobs_cancel).

params.description: Command parameters as a JSON object (see the `params` doc in `command_list`).

wait.description:
Wait for a long command (filters, Content-Aware Fill, Photomerge, …) to finish (default
true). With false it runs as a background job and the result is `{"job": id}`: poll it
with `jobs_list`, stop it with `jobs_cancel`.

brushesView, brushPicker ([x, y] opens the Brush Preset picker there, null closes it),
brushPickerName, brushPickerStroke, brushPickerTip (the picker card's parts, at least one
on), brushPickerScale (the picker footer's card-scale slider, 0.15 to 2, 1 the standard),
brushSize, gradientBlendMode
(a blend mode name, for the Gradient tool), gradientClassic (bool), eyedropperSampleSize
("point" or 1, 3, 5, 11, 31, 51, 101), eyedropperSample (current, currentAndBelow, all,
allNoAdjustments, currentAndBelowNoAdjustments), eyedropperRing (bool), cropOverlay (thirds,
grid, diagonal, triangle, goldenRatio, goldenSpiral), cropOverlayShow (auto, always, never),
cropOverlayOrientation (0..3), cropShield (an object patching show_cropped_area, enabled,
color ("matchCanvas" or "custom"), custom_color ([r, g, b]), opacity (0..100),
auto_adjust, classic_mode and auto_center_preview), cropFill (background or contentAware,
the Crop tool's Fill), shapeStroke (an object patching width, align, cap, join, miterLimit,
dashes, dashOffset and opacity; null disables the stroke). Shape stroke fields use
`shape.edit` names and units; colour comes from `tools.setColors`. camTransformOnDrop (bool,
the Content-Aware Move tool's Transform On Drop). tileGrid (bool, a developer overlay of the
active layer's storage tiles). layerFilter (an object patching by ("kind", "name" or
"mode"), kinds (a list of layer kinds), name (matches part of the layer name) and mode (a
blend mode name) for the Layers panel filter). strokeTrace (true, false, "stderr" or "off":
the stroke latency trace at runtime; a CSV file is set at launch with --stroke-trace, not
over this channel). Other fields are an error.

init.instructions:
SoundCraft is a digital audio workstation (Pro Tools-class). Everything a user can do is a command: call `list_commands` to discover ids and their params, then `execute` (or `batch`). Positions are samples (integers), `{"seconds": x}`, or time strings like "bars_beats:5|1|000" / "0:12.500". Tracks are referenced by id or name. Verify your work with `inspect_session` (tracks, clips, mixer, automation, markers, selection). Programmatic calls never open dialogs. Tools marked APP_ONLY need the desktop app (`soundcraft --control 0` + `soundcraft-cli mcp --connect PORT`).
Backend: headless engine, session `Untitled`.

init.instructions: VectorCraft is a professional vector illustration app. Coordinates are points in document space (y down, origin at the first artboard's top-left; a new document is 612×792). Draw with draw_shape / draw_path, change colours with set_paint, look with render_preview and doc_inspect. Every menu action is a command: find it with command_list and run it with command_run (or command_batch for several). New objects become the selection, and most commands act on the selection (or on explicit `ids`). prompts/list has ready-made workflows, completion/complete finishes a command id, a format, an effect or a swatch name, and vectorcraft://object/{id}, vectorcraft://command/{id}, vectorcraft://effect/{id} and vectorcraft://swatch/{name} read one thing at a time instead of the whole document. Backend: headless.

tools.description: Run steps in order; each edit is its own undo step, or with atomic:true the whole batch is one (named `label`, else after its first edit). A step's id is a command id, or draw_path / draw_shape with that tool's arguments as params (its result is the tool's: the new object's `id`). A param string that is exactly "$N.path" (N: 0-based step index) or "$last.path" takes that value from an earlier step's result, e.g. {"id":"$1.id"}; "$$" starts a literal "$". Returns completed, failed, results and created (the ids draw_path / draw_shape steps made, in order). Stops on the first error by default. At most 256 steps; kept step results total at most 8 MiB, past which the batch stops with the reason.

tools.description: Export the active document with the engine's document.export (the same bytes in the app and headless), in any format of the `format` enum: vectors (svg/svgz with the artboard as viewBox, eps, dxf, emf, wmf), pdf and ai (one page per artboard: all, or `artboard` / `range`; ai is the PDF-compatible .ai file that Save writes, which carries the document when every artboard is written in order), rasters (one rendered artboard: png, jpg, webp, gif, png8 as an indexed .png, tiff, bmp, tga, psd with its layers), txt (the stories, back to front), vectorcraft or template (a native copy or template; the document keeps its path). run_command document.formats lists each format's options. For SVG/SVGZ, top-level `outlineText: true` writes text as paths; DXF takes it too (its type is outlined anyway unless `preserve: editability`). PDF instead uses `options.advanced.outlineText: true`, default false (live text). `selection: true` exports only the selected objects, cropped to their bounds. Template layers are left out; live effects are kept (geometry baked, SVG filters for shadows/glows/blur). Without `path` the bytes come back as dataBase64.

init.instructions: WordCraft is a word processor (a Microsoft Word clone). Every action is a command: find ids and parameters with list_commands and run them with execute (or several with batch). Positions are {story:"body", path:[block,(row,cell,block)...], off:byteOffset}. Typical flow: new_document → type_text "Hello" → execute text.newParagraph → execute para.style {style:"Heading 1"} → select_text {text:"Hello"} → execute format.bold → inspect_document to verify → render_page to look at the result → save {path:"out.docx"}. Backend: headless session (no window). Community: https://discord.gg/artcraft · https://getartcraft.com/apps/wordcraft · https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft
